title: Tyndall AFB: After the Storm
description: Hurricane Michael ripped through the Florida panhandle on Oct. 13, 2018, and Tyndall Air Force Base took a direct hit. These are the stories from the service members involved in the clean up after the storm.

transcript.text: [Air Force Col. Brian S. Laidlaw] By now, you know our base suffered widespread
catastrophic damage.
We're going to need some time to make it safe. We are working this as quickly as we possibly can.
>> Clear prop!
>> Anybody in here?
>> What we have here is the remnants of what used to be aircraft hangars. When Hurricane Michael came through they just blew them
all right over.
We're going to try to clear as much space as we can
and get it out of here from there.
>> Trying to get a good lay of how everything looks whether it's damaged buildings,
damaged roofs,
collapsed buildings and anything we can get the help the guys on the ground
try to secure the surrounding area.
>> When I first showed up to the base, I was not expecting all the damage...
all the knocked over trees, the buildings...
it gave me like shivers down my spine, and
It's one of those things that I know you can't carry your head, you know?
It's like sadness.
>> There has been rumors that there are some squatters, possibly some actual residents of these facilities that
refuse to have gotten out, and what we're doing is we're going there to verify that they have vacated the premises,
and if they are still there, if they require any type of medical attention.
>> Anybody need help?
>> People's homes destroyed, trees through living rooms, it was crazy. It's nothing I've ever seen before.
>> It reminded me of Hurricane Katrina in 2005.
>> This is my chance to really make a difference, and it's one of the most exciting projects I've ever been a part of.
>> Whatever I can do to help, that's all I can ask for.
That's all I've always wanted.
>> We're better off today than we were yesterday, and tomorrow we're going to be better off than we are today.
